title: Robinson's Q is consistent, by exhibiting a model
statement: There is no derivation of falsity from the seven Robinson axioms in the first-order natural-deduction calculus: Not (FO.Provable FO.Q FO.Formula.bot). The proof is soundness applied at the ℕ structure with the constant-zero valuation -- a derivation of bot from Q would give FO.sat Nat FO.natStructureQ FO.Formula.bot v, which iota-reduces to False.

evidence.supports: FO.Q.consistency is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and rests on no axiom. The proof term is one line: fun d => FO.soundness Nat FO.natStructureQ FO.Q FO.Formula.bot d (fun _ => Nat.zero) (FO.Q.natModels (fun _ => Nat.zero)).
evidence.notes: The ℕ structure is doing real work: an arbitrary FO.Structure M would not do, because M could be empty and the argument still needs a valuation Nat -> M to exist. Using a structure whose carrier is inhabited is what makes the corollary constructive.

evidence.supports: The type is rebuilt from FO.Provable, FO.Q and FO.Formula.bot inside the test and compared by Kernel::def_eq rather than by rendering, with a negative control that the SAME statement over FO.Context.nil -- which is fo_soundness.rs's older FO.consistency -- is a DIFFERENT type. So a fact that had silently degraded to the empty-context statement, which is strictly weaker and already landed, is a failure here.

axiom_footprint: [] -- for all 132 declarations build_fo_robinson_prelude adds on top of the Nat prelude, not only the headline theorem. The row set is a SET DIFFERENCE against a kernel carrying only build_nat_prelude, recomputed on every run, so it is derived from the environment rather than from a hand-maintained list. This package is the first that holds BOTH fo_* chains -- the arithmetization (FO.Code.diagAux_code) and the calculus (FO.soundness) -- in one kernel, so the sweep covers both.
evidence.notes: --expect-count fails on drift in EITHER direction, so a declaration silently disappearing is a failure too. The same set difference is recomputed inside the test suite by fo_robinson::tests::the_whole_robinson_package_is_axiom_free, with coverage controls drawn from BOTH chains (FO.Code.diagAux_code and FO.soundness) so it cannot pass vacuously and cannot pass if the two chains stopped composing.

provenance.source: authored from the roadmap item; the axiom list is Robinson's, the encoding, the structure and every proof term are written here

prior_art.what: the finitely axiomatised essentially undecidable arithmetic Q
prior_art.where: R. M. Robinson, 'An essentially undecidable axiom system', Proc. ICM 1950, vol. 1, 729-730
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source

notes: This is the first consistency statement in this repository about a THEORY rather than about the empty context. fo_soundness.rs's FO.consistency says the calculus proves no contradiction from nothing; this says the calculus proves no contradiction from the seven Robinson axioms, which is the statement Goedel's second incompleteness theorem is about. Nothing here approaches that theorem: the proof is model-theoretic and lives in the metatheory, so it is exactly the kind of consistency proof Q cannot carry out about itself.
